thread:
tina_marketing: Hey team, small but urgent ask for launch materials. Need validated numbers + reproducible artifacts for three headline claims: generation p95, embeddings p95, and cost-per-1k-tokens. Prefer a small smoke run today and full sweep early next week. Can runtime take this?

sam_runtime: Yep, we can. Quick checklist so we don't iterate: which exact model tags, which payload pack, sample counts, and do you want cold-starts or steady-state only? Also where should we drop artifacts (embargo S3 path)?

tina_marketing: Models: redwood-alpha-7b:fp16 (tag 2026-03-01) and redwood-alpha-7b:quant8 (tag 2026-03-05). Payload: s3://redwood-internal/marketing/payloads/launch-pack-v4.json. Smoke: 40 samples per model/profile. Full: gen 8k, long-complete 1k, embeds 5k. Include stratified slices (web/mobile/api). Cold-start = first request after 5m idle. Drop artifacts to s3://redwood-internal/marketing/bench-1898765432/ with embargo ACL.

lee_ops: I'll precreate the S3 folder and set ACL to embargo until 2026-04-10. Also add watchers: marketing, platform-metrics.

sam_runtime: Cool. Measurement defs for legal clarity: server-side latency measured at front-end (request receive -> last byte sent), cold-start as you defined, steady-state after 30 warmup requests. We'll output per-request CSV with fields: request_id, model, variant, seq_in, seq_out, tokens, latency_ms, gpu_util_pct, mem_mb, trace_url.

tina_marketing: Legal/communications need acceptance tolerances we can publish: prefer suggested tolerances so legal can sign off quickly.

anya_legal: Suggestion: for public claims, allow p95 tolerance of headline +/- 10% and cost variance <= 15%. Avoid relative language like "identical" for quant unless within 5% latency. Also prefer absolute cold-start numbers rather than percent changes.

sam_runtime: We'll adopt that. Plan: 1) run smoke today with seed=20260325 for determinism, collect 40 samples each; 2) if smoke within tolerance we schedule full sweep Tue night; 3) produce one-line human summaries and a 1-paragraph embargoed blurb + perf CLI commands. Estimated smoke runtime ~90m.

perf-bot: queued bench job bench-1898765432-smoke. ETA 1h30m.

sam_runtime: Command we'll use (for reproducibility):

```
redwood-bench run \
  --model redwood-alpha-7b:fp16 \
  --model redwood-alpha-7b:quant8 \
  --payload s3://redwood-internal/marketing/payloads/launch-pack-v4.json \
  --samples 40 \
  --seed 20260325 \
  --out s3://redwood-internal/marketing/bench-1898765432/smoke/\\
```

perf-bot: bench-1898765432-smoke started 

perf-bot: bench-1898765432-smoke finished 30 summary uploaded to s3://redwood-internal/marketing/bench-1898765432/smoke/summary.csv. Raw traces: s3://redwood-internal/marketing/bench-1898765432/smoke/traces/. Preliminary numbers: 
- redwood-alpha-7b:fp16 (gen p95): 172ms steady-state
- redwood-alpha-7b:quant8 (gen p95): 191ms steady-state (+11% vs fp16)
- embeddings (batch8 p95): 26ms
- cost delta quant8 vs fp16: ~13% lower for this sample workload

tina_marketing: Nice. Can you draft the one-line model summaries and a short embargoed paragraph for the press kit? Also please include a recommended phrasing for legal to use.

sam_runtime: Draft one-liners (prelim):
- redwood-alpha-7b:fp16 3: p95 gen 172ms (steady-state); baseline cost.
- redwood-alpha-7b:quant8 3: p95 gen 191ms (+11%), cost ~13% lower on test workload.
- Embeddings (batch=8): p95 26ms.
Embargoed blurb (1-paragraph, internal): "Internal benchmark on a representative launch payload pack shows redwood-alpha-7B:quant8 reduces per-token compute cost ~13% compared to fp16 at the expense of a modest p95 latency increase in this workload. Results are internal and produced under controlled conditions; see appendix for methodology and raw traces."

anya_legal: That blurb looks fine. Change "modest" to "measured" for tone. Also add a single-sentence methodology link: "See internal appendix: s3://redwood-internal/marketing/bench-1898765432/methodology.txt".

sam_runtime: Updated blurb with wording tweak. Full-sweep scheduling: tentatively Tue 02:00-06:00 in low-traffic window. If marketing approves, we'll reserve burst nodes to ensure job completes in the window. Cost for reserved burst ~2.5k one-time, need ops approval.

tina_marketing: Approve the window. Can finance approve the burst? If not, we'll accept longer run time.

lee_ops: I'll route the burst cost approval. If not approved we'll still run but might extend into the next window.

sam_runtime: Next actions: run full sweep if smoke passes. Deliverables: aggregated CSV, percentile curves PNG, 50 annotated raw traces, run config + seed, perf CLI used, one-line summaries, embargoed blurb, recommended public phrasing with tolerances, and S3 artifact ACL set. We'll also tag the perf job with job id bench-1898765432-full when scheduled.

tina_marketing: Perfect. Please ping #marketing when full-sweep is queued and again when artifacts are available.

perf-bot: tag:complete :white_check_mark:"
